{{short description|Slovenian Marxist philosopher}}
[[File:Božidar Debenjak.jpg|thumbnail|Božidar Debenjak]]
'''Božidar Debenjak''' (born 7 May 1935) is a [[Slovenia]]n [[Marxism|Marxist]] [[philosopher]], [[Social theory|social theorist]] and [[translator]].

==Biography==
He was born in [[Ljubljana]], [[Slovenia]], then part of the [[Kingdom of Yugoslavia]]. In 1961, he became professor at the [[University of Ljubljana]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ff.uni-lj.si/oddelki/filo/vsebina/zgodovina.htm |title=Zgodovina - Oddelek za filozofijo &#124; Filozofska fakulteta &#124; Univerza v Ljubljani |access-date=2010-08-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721021050/http://www.ff.uni-lj.si/oddelki/filo/vsebina/zgodovina.htm |archive-date=2011-07-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref> For more than thirty years, he taught [[Marxism|Marxist theory]] and [[history of philosophy]] at the Ljubljana University; many renowned Slovenian philosophers and sociologists were among his pupils, including [[Slavoj Žižek]], [[Mladen Dolar]], [[Rastko Močnik]], [[Renata Salecl]] and [[Tonči Kuzmanić]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mladina.si/tednik/200904/dr__bozidar_debenjak__filozof|title=MLADINA.si|website=www.mladina.si|accessdate=26 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210152656/http://www.mladina.si/tednik/200904/dr__bozidar_debenjak__filozof|archive-date=10 February 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="primorska.info">{{cite web|url=http://www.primorska.info/docs/4be9192d_001_debenjak.pdf|title=dfltweb1.onamae.com – このドメインはお名前.comで取得されています。|website=www.primorska.info|accessdate=26 November 2018|archive-date=10 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120310224428/http://www.primorska.info/docs/4be9192d_001_debenjak.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was one of the first scholars to introduce the thought of the [[Frankfurt school]] in the curricula of [[SFR Yugoslavia|Yugoslav]] universities.

He has written several books, mostly on Marxist theory, including a monograph on the thought of [[Friedrich Engels]] (''Friedrich Engels: History and Alienation'', 1970), in which he portrayed Engels as a "subtler [[Historical materialism|historical materialist]] than Marx", who "managed to establish a clearer dividing line between history and nature".<ref name="primorska.info"/> His ''Introduction to Marxist Philosophy'' (1977) was published in 4 editions, and was one of the most influential synthesis of Marxist thought in Slovenia.<ref name="primorska.info"/>

He also translated several works, mostly from [[German language|German]], including several works by [[Karl Marx]] (especially [[young Marx]]), [[Friedrich Engels]], [[Rosa Luxemburg]], [[Theodor Adorno]], [[Max Horkheimer]], [[Herbert Marcuse]], [[Karl Korsch]], [[Lenin]], [[Jürgen Habermas]] and [[Martin Luther]]. He also translated [[Hegel]]'s ''[[Phenomenology of the mind|Phenomenology of the Mind]]'' and [[Valvasor]]'s ''[[The Glory of the Duchy of Carniola]]'' (together with [[Doris Debenjak|his wife]] and son), and co-authored one of the most comprehensive Slovene-German dictionaries.<ref>http://www.emka.si/veliki-slovensko-nemski-slovar-grosses-slowenisch-deutsches-w%C3%B6rterbuch/PR/36182,56{{dead link|date=November 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

He was married to [[Doris Debenjak]] (née Krisch), a Slovenian translator of [[Gottscheers|Gottschee German]] descent and chair of the [[Society of Native Gottschee Settlers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mladina.si/tednik/200504/clanek/nar--cenzura-peter_petrovcic/|title=Moderna grmada - MLADINA.si|publisher=|accessdate=26 November 2018}}</ref>

== Major works==
*''Pota razvoja'' ("Paths of Development". Ljubljana, 1961).
*''Friedrich Engels - zgodovina in odtujitev'' ("Friedrich Engels: History and Alienation". Maribor, 1970).
*''V alternativi : marksistične študije'' ("In Alternative: Marxist Studies". Ljubljana, 1974).
*''Meščanski kozmos in revolucionarna teorija: aspekti "kritične teorije družbe"'' ("The Bourgeois Universe and the Revolutionary Theory: Aspects of the 'Critical Theory of Society'. Ljubljana, 1977).
*''Vstop v marksistično filozofijo'' ("Introduction to Marxist Philosophy". Ljubljana, 1977).
